etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowing from Latin ēbulliēns, present participle of ēbulliō (“to boil”), from bulliō (“to bubble up”) (English boil). Compare bubbling, bubbly, and perky, which use a similar metaphor.
senses: (archaic) Of a liquid: boiling and bubbling, or agitated as if boiling.
